name: TPG Inc.

profile.description: TPG Inc., founded in 1992 and headquartered in Fort Worth, Texas, is a global alternative asset manager. Its platforms span private equity, growth, impact (Rise), credit and real estate (Angelo Gordon), and market solutions [4]. At Q3 2026, AUM was $345.7B (+21% YoY), fee-paying AUM was $190B (+16%), and dry powder reached a record $86B. Fee-related earnings were $321M at a ~50% margin, and after-tax distributable earnings were $0.65 per share [1][2]. TPG has been public since its January 2022 IPO.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Since its 2022 IPO, TPG has grown from a PE-centric firm into a multi-platform manager. The Angelo Gordon credit and real-estate business helped lift AUM to $345.7B (+21% YoY), and FRE rose ~43% YoY in Q3 2026 [1][2]. AI Deployment (0/2): Searches found no AI-powered products shipped to clients and no quantified internal AI savings. Market Share (1/2): TPG is a top-tier alternative manager, but at $346B it is well behind Blackstone, Apollo and KKR, and no share-gain data was found. Pipeline (1/2): Record $86B of dry powder and 16% fee-paying AUM growth give fee visibility, but no dated fund-launch timelines were found [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D line is reported, which is typical for asset managers [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): TPG frames itself around innovation-led investing. The Rise impact platform gives it more purpose than peers, but the firm-wide mission is not distinctive. Community Impact (1/2): TPG adopted a Global ESG Performance Policy in 2012 and signed the UN Principles for Responsible Investment in 2013, years before most peers, per its S-1 [5]. No dollar-quantified community programs were found in this screen. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor ratings run ~3.0-3.6 with only 51% recommending the firm. Reviewers cite a 'boys club' culture and say it has declined since leadership hires from Goldman Sachs [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): No net open-market insider buying was found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically on the Growth template. GAAP metrics are noisy for an alternative manager. TTM ROE of 21.9% and the 5-year GAAP revenue CAGR of 15.6% ($2.27B in 2020 to $4.67B in 2025) both clear their targets [3][4]. FY2025 GAAP revenue growth of +77.9% is inflated by capital allocations; the cleaner FRE grew ~43% YoY in Q3 2026 [1][4]. Forward P/E of ~13.6 is self-derived ($48.18 price over FY2027 consensus EPS of $3.55) [7]. FMP's forward PEG of 1.62 scores 0.69 at double weight [3]. The drags are D/E of 168.6% and a GAAP net margin of only 5.2%, which reflects non-controlling interests and equity-based compensation [3]. Liquidity of ~$140M/day is ample.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Alternative asset management depends on relationship-driven fundraising from pensions and sovereign wealth funds, negotiation of complex control transactions, and fiduciary judgment. These are protected by regulation and trust, and AI cannot easily replicate them. The secondary risk is indirect: AI disruption of software and services portfolio companies could pressure fund marks and carried interest. No analyst commentary specifically flags TPG's model as AI-vulnerable. AI Opportunity (0/1): TPG discloses no AI product revenue.

infinite_game.summary: TPG's early ESG commitments (2012 policy, 2013 UN PRI signatory) and the Rise impact platform show a genuine purpose beyond returns [5]. As a public company, however, the firm is now visibly optimized for AUM growth, FRE margin targets (~48% for 2026), and fundraising scale [2]. Employee reviews describe an elitist, Goldman-heavy culture [6]. Through Sinek's lens, TPG plays a mostly finite game with an infinite-minded sleeve.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The Rise platform and early ESG adoption show a cause beyond profit that predated market trends [5]. It defines one platform, not the whole firm.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor reviewers describe a 'boys club' culture, 'rampant elitism' and a culture that 'tanked' after senior Goldman Sachs hires, with only 51% recommending the firm [6]. Leadership continuity under Jon Winkelried (co-CEO 2015, sole CEO since 2021) is the offsetting positive [6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that frames Blackstone, KKR or Apollo as rivals to learn from. Messaging centers on AUM, fundraising and FRE margin targets [2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): TPG evolved from a private partnership into a public, multi-platform manager by adding credit and real estate through Angelo Gordon [4]. This is substantial but adjacent evolution.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Adopting ESG policies in 2012 and building a dedicated impact franchise were early, contrarian commitments [5]. Recent capital allocation is more conventional and growth-focused.

investment_thesis: TPG is compounding its fee base. Q3 2026 AUM rose 21% to $345.7B, fee-paying AUM grew 16% to $190B, FRE rose ~43% YoY at a ~50% margin, and record dry powder of $86B should convert into management fees as it is deployed [1][2]. At $48 (well off the $70 52-week high) the stock trades at ~13.6x FY2027 consensus EPS, with a 4.65% dividend yield and consensus EPS rising from $2.79 (2026) to $4.28 (2028) [3][7].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that GAAP economics are far weaker than distributable earnings. The GAAP net margin is 5.2%, the TTM P/E is 32.8x, and D/E is 168.6% [3]. Q3 fee-related revenue grew only ~1.6% sequentially, and normalized FRE margin was ~47% excluding $62M of catch-up fees [1][2]. Realizations and carried interest depend on exit markets. The firm also faces greenwashing and anti-ESG political risk to fundraising, as flagged in its own 10-K [5].
key_catalysts: Deployment of the record $86B dry powder converting into fee-paying AUM and carried interest
FRE margin expansion toward management's ~48% 2026 guidance on a normalized basis
Exit-market recovery driving realizations and higher distributable earnings per share
key_risks: Normalized FRE margin (~47%) below the headline 50%; fee-related revenue growth stalling sequentially
Leverage: GAAP debt-to-equity of 168.6% and payout well above GAAP earnings
Anti-ESG and greenwashing regulatory risk to the impact-investing brand
AI disruption of software/services portfolio companies pressuring fund marks
